title: Motion of Dissipative Solitons in Quasi-One-Dimensional Potentials
content: We consider the motion of two-dimensional (2D) dissipative solitons and soliton pairs in the framework of the cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation with quasi-1D potentials, spatially periodic or radial-lattice ones. The equation is solved numerically for inputs representing one or two fundamental solitons, which are set in motion by a kick. For the quasi-1D potential, the kick parallel to the potential axis naturally initiates free motion of the 2D solitons, as the model remains Galilean-invariant in this direction. Motion in the transverse direction, which may entail pulse multiplication, commences if the kick is strong enough. Oblique kicks lead to a straightforward superposition of the longitudinal and transverse motions. Also considered is the collision between 2D solitons moving in the longitudinal and diagonal directions. In the radial potential, the soliton kicked towards the center may bounce back from the central potential hill or pass it, producing complex trajectories and splitting of the moving soliton.
